fields.meta_title: Online Dental Intake Form Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Create a dental intake form that collects x-ray dates and medical history before the first visit, with comfort notes for the hygienist. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Dental Intake Form the Dentist Reads Before the Visit
fields.hero_description: Build a dental intake form that sends each new patient's history and visit reason to a database you own before the appointment.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Asks Before the Patient Sits Down
fields.features_subheading: A dental intake form built here asks for the dates and signatures the front desk and the dentist use before the first exam.
fields.feature_1:
A reason for the visit, picked then described

Open the form with one question: what brings the patient in. A pick list covers routine reasons like a cleaning or a toothache, and a text box below it takes the details in full.
fields.feature_2:
Dental history with dates, not guesses

Ask when the patient last had a cleaning and last had x-rays, each as a month and a year. The previous office's name and phone number sit next to those dates on the record.
fields.feature_3:
A medical history list your dentist approves

Show the conditions and allergies your dentist wants to know about as checkboxes. Medications go in as rows, one per medicine with its dose, which puts each one on its own line.
fields.feature_4:
A signature under the office policies

Place the financial policy and the cancellation policy on the last screen, each with a checkbox. The patient signs once with an e-signature, and the app saves it on the record.
fields.feature_5:
Reminder emails for unfinished intakes

Pick how many days before the visit a reminder goes out. A patient who has not finished the form gets an email with the link, and the front desk sees who is still missing.
fields.feature_6:
Code your practice can take anywhere

On paid plans, export the full code of the intake app to your GitHub repository. A developer can then place the form on the practice website or change where the records are stored.

fields.usecase_heading: Where Four Dental Offices Use the Answers
fields.tab_content_1:
Before the 11:40 toothache visit, three answers wait

Bastian Thibodeaux called Tannery Row Dental about a toothache and took the 11:40 same-day slot. His confirmation email links to a short emergency intake. He marks the lower left side, pain for 2 days, and pain with cold drinks. Dr. Ilona Ferrante reads those three answers on a card before he sits down.
fields.tab_content_2:
Records to request, sorted by last x-ray date

Marguerite Asante switched to Pembrook Avenue Dental from an office across town. On the intake, she gives March 2025 as the date of her last x-rays. Office manager Ezra Pennimore sees this week's new patients sorted by that date, oldest first. Her name is on his list of 3 records to request.
fields.tab_content_3:
For the 2:15 cleaning, a pause signal and headphones

Teodora Wilkes put her nerves at 4 out of 5 on Corrie Lane Dental's intake. The next question asks what helps, and she picks a raised hand to pause and headphones during the cleaning. Hygienist Linnea Sorensen sees both on the card for the 2:15 appointment, before Teodora reaches the chair.
fields.tab_content_4:
Spanish on screen, English labels for staff

Rafael Ibarrola tapped Spanish on the first screen of Vireo Dental's intake. His choices fill the same fields as the English form, so the record shows English labels. Front desk lead Yesenia Castellar sees Language: Spanish at the top and books the Spanish-speaking assistant for his 9:00 visit.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Dental Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps take a dental intake form from your current paper packet to a link new patients finish before the exam.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pull the questions out of your packet
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Get the medical history list approved
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Collect medications one row at a time
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the reason for the visit, then go through your current new patient packet page by page. Write down every question on it, and mark the ones nobody at the front desk or the chair reads before an exam.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Replace yes or no history questions with dates. A patient whose last x-rays were in March 2025 should enter that month, not tick a box for the last two years. Keep the section short: two dates and where the patient went before.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Turn the conditions the dentist wants flagged into checkboxes, then have the dentist read the full list before it goes live. The dentist decides what the form asks, and Emergent builds the form from the questions you give it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give each medication its own row with the name, the dose, and how often the patient takes it. Ask about allergies to medicines and to materials such as latex as a separate question. Neither answer then gets lost in a long text box.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Copy the exact wording of each office policy from the documents your practice uses today, and have the office manager confirm it is the current version. Each policy then gets its own checkbox above the e-signature on the last screen.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Describe the form in one prompt
fields.howto_step_6_des: Put the sections in order in one prompt, with the reminder timing and who sees which answers. Emergent then builds the patient records behind the form, plus a card for each person who reads the answers. Change any part later by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Book a fake patient and fill out the intake on a phone, the way a patient would from the confirmation email. Check that each answer reaches the right card and the reminder email arrives, then send the link with real bookings.

faq_plan.q: What is a dental intake form?
faq_plan.a: A dental intake form is the set of questions a dental office asks a new patient before the first exam. It collects contact details, the reason for the visit, dental and medical history, medications and allergies, and a signature on the office policies. The office reads the answers before the patient reaches the chair.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a dental intake form?
faq_plan.a: List the questions your dentist wants answered, group them into sections, and describe the form in a prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it. Fill it out yourself on a phone as a fake patient, then send the link in each booking confirmation.

faq_plan.q: How do I turn a paper dental intake form template into an online form?
faq_plan.a: Copy its questions into a list, cross out the ones your dentist never reads, and add any your packet lacks. Then describe the sections in order in a prompt. Emergent builds the online version from that list, and a section you add later is one more prompt. Keep the paper dental intake form template only as a checklist.

faq_plan.q: How is a dental intake form different from other healthcare intake forms?
faq_plan.a: The difference is in the dental sections, such as the dates of the last cleaning and the last x-rays. The contact and signature sections can match a pt intake form or any other healthcare intake. Reuse those as they are and spend your time on the dental questions and the reason for the visit.

faq_plan.q: How should medical history questions be laid out on a dental intake form?
faq_plan.a: Lay them out as a checklist the dentist has approved, one condition per checkbox, with a details box that opens on a yes. Keep medications and allergies as separate questions below the checklist. A patient then reads short items instead of one long paragraph, and staff can scan the yes answers first.

faq_plan.q: When should new patients get dental intake forms before the first visit?
faq_plan.a: Send the link at booking, in the confirmation email, and remind anyone who has not finished 2 days before the visit. That gives the front desk time to request records from the previous office. The app emails the reminder and shows staff which patients are still missing a form.

faq_plan.q: Can a dental intake form ask patients what makes them comfortable?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a short section that asks how nervous the patient feels on a 1 to 5 scale and what helps, such as a signal to pause or numbing explained first. Treat these answers like the preferences on a massage intake form: they go on the hygienist's card, apart from the medical history.

faq_plan.q: How do returning patients update a dental intake form?
faq_plan.a: Send returning patients a review screen with their saved answers instead of a blank form. They change what is new, such as a medication or an address, and confirm the rest. Ask Emergent to add the review step, and each update stays on the same patient record in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can patients sign a dental intake form on their phone?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The app captures an e-signature on a phone screen, below the office policies on the last page, and saves it on the patient record. Have whoever owns your policies decide which ones need a signature and confirm the wording before the form goes live.

faq_plan.q: How long should a dental intake form take to fill out?
faq_plan.a: Only as long as the questions someone at the practice reads before the exam. Time it yourself on a phone, and cut any question whose answer nobody opens. The same test works for a therapy intake form or any other intake. Forms Emergent builds have no response caps, and length is a choice made for the patient, not a plan limit.

plan.angle: The top 10 is dental offices posting their own new patient PDFs, one university clinic's online form, two dental form vendors and one blog on why intake matters. Each shows one practice's paperwork. This page shows what a dental intake form collects for the dentist's chair (the reason for the visit, the date of the last x-rays, the medical history and medications the dentist reviews, comfort preferences) and four moments where the answers get used: a same-day toothache, a patient switching from another office, a nervous patient's cleaning, and a patient who fills the form in Spanish.
